title: Conestoga College transit hub and U-Pass agreements
subtitle: Mobility Plus targets and software, Oxford Road 5 deferral, and a tied vote on townhome waste rebate.
overview: The Planning and Works Committee recommended a design concept for a new Grand River Transit hub at Conestoga College's Doon campus, along with added engineering consulting funds. It also recommended new U-Pass agreements with Conestoga College and its student union, and extended agreements with Wilfrid Laurier University, the University of Waterloo graduate students and others, running to August 2027.

On Mobility Plus, the specialized transit service, the committee recommended a 2024 target of 2.5% undelivered trips and asked staff to report in-year on speeding up a scheduling software upgrade. Residents who rely on the service may see fewer missed trips.

A motion on taking over Oxford Road 5 was deferred to March 5, 2024, until staff report on the road assumption policy. A motion asking for a report on bringing back the waste rebate for townhome complexes without truck access was defeated on a tie {{vote:m7}}. Staff said a multi-residential waste study is already planned within the waste management master plan.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the design concept for the Conestoga College Transit Hub and raising the Arcadis consulting agreement by $357,000 to a revised upset limit of $590,100 plus taxes {{vote:m3}}.

The committee recommended a U-Pass agreement with Conestoga Students Inc. and Conestoga College, extensions of existing university agreements to August 31, 2027, and an interim fee schedule with annual increases for 2025/2026 and 2026/2027.
The committee recommended a 2.5% target for undelivered Mobility Plus trips in 2024, with staff continuing to report quarterly {{vote:m4}}.
The committee directed staff to report back in-year on the operating and capital investments needed to speed up the scheduling software upgrade {{vote:m5}}.
The committee deferred the Oxford Road 5 motion to the March 5, 2024 meeting, after a staff report on the road assumption policy {{vote:m6}}.
A motion asking staff to report by April 9, 2024 on reinstating the waste rebate for townhome complexes lacking truck access was defeated {{vote:m7}}.

debate: A student association delegate supported the Conestoga hub, citing safety, traffic flow and climate-friendly travel. A Doon resident delegate said too many real-life questions remained unanswered, including speeding and crossing the road, and worried the hub serves mainly the college.

Staff said the current terminal is the busiest transfer point and is out of capacity. They said moving it toward the roadway serves both students and community riders, and that the City of Kitchener plans to rebuild the road with pedestrian crossing points.

On Oxford Road 5, the sponsor said the road meets the upload criteria and that talks had gone on for over three years. Staff said the policy review should come first. One councillor asked for the full cost, including reconstruction and ongoing operating costs.

On the townhome rebate, the sponsor argued for equitable service where trucks cannot reach complexes. Staff said the rebate was ended in 2021 and a multi-residential study is planned within the master plan. They added that separating townhomes could take longer. Other councillors questioned whether the motion would deliver equity, and one noted that rebates often went to owners rather than residents.
